LEVEL 1 · FOUNDATION
The Lantern With Two Handles
Nuri wants to carry the lantern all by herself. But her arm gets tired. What can two friends do with one light?
Jurassic English · Original Stories · Level 1 Foundation

Chapter 1 · A light for the walk
Nuri and Bo make a lantern.
Nuri puts yellow paper on it. Bo adds blue stars.
Grandad puts a little battery light inside.
‘Ready for the garden walk?’ he asks.
‘Ready!’ they say.
Bo asks: What does Bo add to the lantern?
1

Chapter 2 · My turn
‘I can carry it,’ says Nuri.
She holds the handle.
Bo walks beside her. Grandad walks behind them.
The light makes a yellow spot on the path.
Nuri holds it up high.
Grandad asks: Who carries the lantern first?
2

Workbook 4 · The Jurassic Thinking Cycle
1 Analyze
Page 3 · A tired hand
How do you know Nuri needs help? Find the clue on this page.
The light drops low. · She runs very fast. · She sings a song.
2 Evaluate
Page 4 · A question
Nuri asks Bo for help. Is that a good choice?
Yes · Not sure · No
3 Justify
Page 4 · A question
Tell why. Use because. You can say it, point or write.
I think it is a good choice because ___.
Word bank: tired · help · Bo · together · handle · light
4 Reflect
Page 6 · Their light
When do you ask for help? Who can you ask? Draw or tell.

LEVEL 1 · FOUNDATION
Mina and the Midnight Drum
Mina loves the big drum. Her friend Sami needs a quieter sound. Can they find a song for both of them?
Jurassic English · Original Stories · Level 1 Foundation

Chapter 1 · The big drum
Mina has a small drum.
BOOM! Her aunt plays the big drum.
It is the Midnight Drum. It will play at the town party.
Mina smiles. ‘Can I play?’
Mina asks: Who plays the big drum first?
1

Chapter 2 · A sound too big
Mina hits the drum.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Her friend Sami puts his hands over his ears.
‘Too big,’ he says.
Mina stops. Her smile stops too.
Sami asks: What does Sami do when Mina hits the drum?
2

Chapter 3 · Two different needs
‘I want to play,’ says Mina.
‘I want to listen,’ says Sami. ‘But not so loud.’
Auntie sits with them.
‘We can try a small sound,’ she says.
Auntie asks: What does Sami want?
3

Chapter 4 · The soft sticks
Auntie brings two soft drumsticks.
Mina taps.
Tum. Tum.
Sami takes his hands down.
‘I can hear you,’ he says.
Mina smiles again.
Sami asks: What does Auntie bring?
4

Chapter 5 · One more song?
They play a little song.
Then Sami yawns.
‘One more?’ asks Mina.
Sami shakes his head.
‘I feel tired.’
Mina looks at the drum. Then she puts the sticks down.
Mina asks: What does Sami do after the little song?
5

Chapter 6 · A song for tomorrow
Mina draws two drums on a card.
‘Our song. Tomorrow,’ she writes with Auntie.
Sami adds a little moon.
They leave the drums to rest.
Outside, Mina hums. Sami hums too.
A small song is enough tonight.
Sami asks: What does Sami add to the card?
6
